## Question and chemical basis

Replace this paragraph with your explanation of the absorbing species, why we
measure at 510 nm, and the concentration basis. These are simulated teaching
data. The intended measurand is mg Fe/L in the supplied filtered water under
the assumed quantitative reduction and complex formation conditions.

## Spectrum and calibration

```{r import}
spectra <- read_csv("data/spectra.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
standards <- read_csv("data/standards.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
readings <- read_csv("data/readings.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
preparations <- read_csv("data/preparations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
qc <- read_csv("data/qc.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fit <- lm(absorbance ~ standard_mg_l, data = standards)
a <- unname(coef(fit)[1])
b <- unname(coef(fit)[2])
coef(fit)
```

```{r spectrum, fig.cap="Simulated spectral series; each trace is one solution, not multiple independent samples."}
ggplot(spectra, aes(wavelength_nm, absorbance, colour = trace)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Absorbance", colour = "Solution") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r calibration, fig.cap="Independent final calibration solutions, measured at 510 nm."}
ggplot(standards, aes(standard_mg_l, absorbance)) +
  geom_point() + geom_abline(intercept = a, slope = b) +
  labs(x = "Iron in final solution (mg Fe/L)", y = "Absorbance at 510 nm") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r residuals, fig.cap="Observed minus fitted response at each calibration concentration."}
standards <- standards |> mutate(residual = residuals(fit))
ggplot(standards, aes(standard_mg_l, residual)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") + geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Iron in final solution (mg Fe/L)", y = "Residual absorbance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Explain what supports using a straight line and what the residuals cannot tell
us about the sample matrix. Explain the units of the slope and why an
intercept was fitted.

## Independent check and range

```{r quality-control}
qc_summary <- qc |>
  group_by(block) |>
  summarise(mean_absorbance = mean(absorbance),
            reference_mg_l = first(reference_mg_l), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(estimated_mg_l = (mean_absorbance - a) / b,
         recovery_percent = 100 * estimated_mg_l / reference_mg_l,
         qc_pass = recovery_percent >= 95 & recovery_percent <= 105)
knitr::kable(qc_summary, digits = 3)
```

This exercise uses a supplied 95–105% check recovery window. Explain the
consequence of each block's check result.

```{r match-and-calculate}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(preparations$preparation_id),
          all(readings$preparation_id %in% preparations$preparation_id))
response_limits <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(standard_mg_l = c(0, 4)))
results <- readings |>
  group_by(preparation_id) |>
  summarise(m = n(), mean_absorbance = mean(absorbance),
            in_range = all(absorbance >= response_limits[1] &
                           absorbance <= response_limits[2]), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(preparations, by = "preparation_id") |>
  left_join(qc_summary |> select(block, qc_pass), by = "block") |>
  mutate(reportable = in_range & qc_pass,
         final_mg_l = if_else(reportable,
                              (mean_absorbance - a) / b, NA_real_),
         dilution_factor = final_ml / aliquot_ml,
         original_mg_l = final_mg_l * dilution_factor,
         decision = case_when(!qc_pass ~ "Withhold: QC failed",
                              !in_range ~ "Remeasure: outside range",
                              TRUE ~ "Report under stated assumptions"))
knitr::kable(results |> select(preparation_id, sample_id, dilution_factor,
                              original_mg_l, decision), digits = 3)
write_csv(results, "output/student-concentrations.csv", na = "NA")
```

Explain why P04 supports a W2 result whereas P03 does not. Explain why matching
by row order would fail, and why `NA` is not zero iron. P01 and P02 are separate
preparations of the same collected sample, not independent water samples.

## P01 uncertainty

```{r uncertainty}
p01_readings <- readings |> filter(preparation_id == "P01")
u_p01 <- inverse_calibration(fit, p01_readings$absorbance)
p01 <- results |> filter(preparation_id == "P01")
u_original <- sqrt(
  (p01$dilution_factor * u_p01$u_cal_mg_l)^2 +
  (p01$original_mg_l * p01$u_final_ml / p01$final_ml)^2 +
  (p01$original_mg_l * p01$u_aliquot_ml / p01$aliquot_ml)^2)
knitr::kable(u_p01, digits = 5)
u_original
```

P01 gave `r sprintf("%.3f", p01$original_mg_l)` mg Fe/L with a standard
uncertainty of `r sprintf("%.3f", u_original)` mg Fe/L from the stated model.
Explain why this is neither a full method uncertainty nor a 95% interval.
State the helper's assumptions and the omitted sources of uncertainty.
